transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brought you in today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Um, mostly I’m here because I’m just... I'm tired in a way that sleep doesn’t really fix. Like, even doing basic stuff, like unloading the dishwasher, can feel like it's just way too much. Which is annoying because I just bought those new detergent pods? They were on sale at Target, but honestly, I think they leave a weird film on the glasses. My mom always said powder was better, but who wants to deal with measuring that out every time? 

But yeah, I'm just so drained. Even reading for my certificate class is too much right now. I'm taking it online since I'm trying to finish up some college stuff, and the instructor is this guy who wears these really loud, patterned bowties. He always starts his lectures with a joke that isn't funny at all, and it’s just really distracting, especially when you're already so exhausted that just looking at the screen feels impossible, you know?
How long have you been feeling this constantly drained, low-energy way—days, weeks, or longer?

Well, this quieter stretch... just feeling so depressed and heavy with all this fatigue... it's been going on for about three months now. Which I know for sure because it started right around the time my sister adopted her labradoodle. They named him Barnaby, which I told her sounds like an old British man who drinks tea and solves mysteries, not a dog. She bought him these little argyle sweaters anyway, and they're cute, I guess, but they get dirty so fast when he goes in the mud. I haven't even gone over to see him much because I just have zero interest in doing anything, you know? I'm just too exhausted to even drive over there. But yeah, it's been about three months of feeling this way.
Have you ever had a period lasting several days where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than usual?

Um, yeah, actually... before this whole tired phase started, there was a stretch for a few weeks where I felt just... unusually lit up. Like, I was just so sure everything was going to be absolutely amazing. I had all these ideas and was planning all these updates for the house. 

Which, by the way, we live in this older ranch-style place, and the people who lived there before us painted the brick fireplace this awful salmon pink color. Who does that? It’s like they wanted the living room to look like a seafood buffet. I was looking at all these masonry paints to fix it, and they have so many shades of white now—eggshell, ivory, alabaster. It's actually really overwhelming when you get to the hardware store because the little swatches all look exactly the same under those fluorescent lights. 

But anyway, even though I felt so great and energized, I was also... I don't know, just really quick to get mad? Like, I would just snap at my husband over the tiniest things. If he made even a small comment about the budget, or what I was doing with the house, I would just bite his head off. Which is honestly a little hypocritical of him because he's the one who insists on buying name-brand paper towels. If we're going to argue about the budget, why are we spending three extra dollars on something that literally just goes in the trash? The store brand absorbs water just fine. But yeah... I did have a few weeks where I was super energized but also just really irritable with him like that.
During these past three months of feeling drained, have you noticed things like feeling unusually cold, dry skin, hair thinning, or weight gain that you can't explain?

Um, no, not really. I haven't noticed being cold, and my weight is pretty much exactly the same. My skin is fine, I think? I mean, my hair definitely needs a cut, but it's not falling out or thinning or anything. 

It's just getting really long and unmanageable right now because my regular stylist, Jessica, just up and moved to Austin. Which is honestly so annoying because she’s the only one who knows how to do my layers right without making me look like a mushroom. She told me they moved down there for the music scene, but I'm pretty sure it's just because her boyfriend got a job at one of those tech start-ups. He works for a company that makes an app to remind you to water your houseplants? Which is just so silly to me, because you can literally just stick your finger in the dirt to see if it's dry. Why do we need an app on our phones to tell us how dirt feels? And I guess they charge like five dollars a month for a subscription to it! I told my husband, if we're arguing about the budget for paper towels, we definitely aren't subscribing to a plant app. 

But yeah, no, my hair is totally normal, just needs a trim. And I haven't had any of those other things you mentioned.
